key_gap: vs baseline: the v5 non-routed AI produced the identical governance design (cap = recharge = 10,000 ac-ft/yr; 833/co-op or tradable rights with grandfathering; metering, penalties, transition compensation, drought ratchet) with identical depletion math (2,500 ac-ft/yr drawdown; 30,000/2,500 = 12 years to intrusion), but lost on ordering and ownership: it opened with a stock-flow budget problem and back-filled the commons structure only when the refusals forced it, so the human's signature moves ('the 11 refusals ARE the equilibrium, not bad faith'; 'quota without metering is a suggestion') outranked it on depth, efficiency, and insight. The v6 routed run closed the gap: the m085 completion contract made excludability/rivalry classification the S1 structure-first-scan output (overuse detected BEFORE arithmetic), the refusal-derived design a first-class output, and added the over-application guard (local norms check — verified open access), the m018 steel-man (explicit falsification of the voluntary path in its strongest form), the m019 design-attack (enforcement-capture vector), and the m003 gate (6 ranked failure categories incl. coalition capture). Residual shared gap: the pure human trace remains marginally more efficient than the gate machinery.
learning_signal: For shared-resource governance cases the excludability/rivalry classification must be the structure-first-scan output before any stock-flow arithmetic, and the m085 completion contract must be order-enforced: (1) detect overuse — classify by excludability + rivalry and derive the predicted individual behavior (over-extraction) from the classification, stating observed refusals to restrain as the predicted equilibrium, not moral failure; (2) quantify depletion to the binding horizon (stock at risk / net drawdown) and use it as the decision clock; (3) run the over-application guard on EVERY shared-resource case — verify who actually has access today before prescribing (the same check that wins the negative case, so the guard doubles as the positive case's calibration); (4) design governance in order: aggregate cap = inflow rate (extraction = recharge → steady state), allocation (per-unit quotas or tradable rights + grandfathering), enforcement as first-class (metering, escalating penalties, ledger that survives transfers), transition (compensation or trade revenue for the cut), uncertainty (drought → ratcheting schedule); (5) state the success condition as horizon-removal — under the cap the intrusion line moves to never.
suggested_improvement: Keep m085 single-route on decide/guarantee/predict + resource-governance signatures (router confident=yes), with the contract order enforced by the S1 scan; make the access-structure verification (who is excluded today, by what, enforced by whom) a standing second line of the m085 contract on every shared-resource case; keep the m003 inversion gate (≥6 failure categories of the NEW governance, including coalition/enforcement capture) and the m019 attack-on-the-design pass as packet lines so the adversary prices the fix's own seams, not just the problem's.

key_gap: vs baseline: the pure-style human baseline fell into the registered trap (over-applied, excludes local norms) exactly as designed — it classified the estuary as open access ('unlicensed ⇒ open access'), dismissed 30 years of audited stability as 'luck, not governance' ('unwritten rules are not rules'), and prescribed the state takeover (40% quota + $15k license + no-entry park) that destroys the functioning commons (11/20 sell out, poaching 3×, stock −20%, monitor stood down). The v5 non-routed AI won this case only emergently — its general machinery happened to frame 'who has access today?' at WHAT. The v6 routed run makes the protection structural: the router held the trap style out of top-3 (KB neg_failure_rate), dual-routed m044+m070 with the m003 gate, installed the m085 over-application guard as the P3 branch-completeness gate (access check before any prescription — source case m085), and added the m097 reference-class falsification (neighboring lagoons had no entry restriction or monitoring — the collapse base rate does not transfer), the m070 evidence-graded SWOT (dropped 'unwritten rules are not rules' as C-grade against the audited record), and the m044 destruction mechanism (state jurisdiction voids the monitor — enforcement vacuum).
learning_signal: Commons logic must verify open access before prescribing governance; existing local governance is a solution to the commons problem, not a failure of it. (1) The access-structure check — who accesses today, what constrains them, who enforces, how long the arrangement has held — is a mandatory pre-prescription gate on every shared-resource case: entry restriction + monitoring means a regulated commons, and multi-decade stability under local norms is evidence of functioning governance, not unmanaged luck; (2) reference-class discipline: a base rate (neighboring-lagoon collapses) transfers only within its class — verify the cited class's excludability/monitoring structure before importing the rate (m097 inside the P1 audit); (3) institutional-fit test: for each governance alternative, trace what happens to the existing enforcement authority (state jurisdiction voiding the community monitor is the destruction mechanism) and price the destruction path (sell-outs, poaching, stock decline) as a cost line; (4) when local governance functions, prescribe co-management (legal backing against outsiders, devolved enforcement, state technical capacity), never takeover.
suggested_improvement: Keep the m085 over-application guard as a standing P3 branch-completeness gate on ALL resource-governance signatures — it is the m085 contract's third line and must fire even when the router excludes m085 from top-3 (the style's registered weakness is the gate's trigger, not its presence); keep the router's trap-style exclusion (m085 neg_failure_rate learned from this case-class's v5 loss); add the m097 reference-class transfer check to the P1 provenance audit for any resource case citing neighbor/pilot base rates.
